aiSummary.oneLiner: A collection of leaked or reverse-engineered system prompts and model details from popular AI tools.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This repository archives the foundational system prompts and model configurations used by prominent commercial AI tools and applications. It aims to demystify how companies construct the initial context and behavioral guardrails for their AI features. By examining these system prompts, developers can learn advanced prompt engineering techniques, such as how to define rigid personas, enforce output formats, and prevent jailbreaks. The collection serves as an educational resource for understanding the hidden instructions that drive user-facing AI interactions. It provides a rare look under the hood of production-grade AI systems.
keyFeatures: Production prompt archive: Collects the actual system instructions used by successful commercial AI applications.
Model configuration details: Documents which specific underlying models and parameters these tools employ.
Reverse-engineering insights: Showcases techniques used by researchers to extract these hidden prompts.
Advanced prompt patterns: Reveals how industry leaders structure complex instructions and behavioral guardrails.
Educational resource: Provides concrete examples for developers looking to build their own robust AI agents.

useCases.title: Studying Prompt Architecture
useCases.description: AI developers can analyze the collected prompts to learn how to structure complex, multi-part instructions for their own tools.

useCases.title: Improving AI Guardrails
useCases.description: Security researchers can review the prompts to understand how commercial tools attempt to prevent abuse and jailbreaking.

useCases.title: Replicating Tool Behavior
useCases.description: Engineers can use the archived prompts as a starting point to build open-source alternatives with similar functionality.

useCases.title: Analyzing Model Selection
useCases.description: Product managers can evaluate which specific LLM models successful tools are choosing for different tasks.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: This repository is for AI researchers, prompt engineers, and developers who want to study production-grade AI architectures. It is highly valuable for anyone looking to improve the reliability and safety of their own LLM applications.
aiSummary.gettingStarted: Clone the repository and browse the markdown files for specific tools.
